newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heating oil ends off on increasing supplies.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heating oil ends off on increasing supplies.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil ended lower on Friday as refiners and marketers scrambled to ship an increasing supply of distillate on the Colonial Pipeline.
"The Colonial allocation kept the pressure on heating oil despite colder weather in the East Coast," said Tom Bentz, analyst with ING Derivatives in New York.

January heating oil lost 0.81 cent to settle at 72.97 cents a gallon. On Thursday, Colonial Pipeline Co said it extended space allocations through January 1997, still faced with more shipping demand than its huge Houston-to-New York distillate line can handle, a Colonial official said.
The official also said he "would not be surprised" if Colonial again extended the allocations through February.

Moreover, about 120,000 tonnes of Russian gas oil is due to arrive in the United States in the next week, in addition to a previously reported 60,000 tonne vessel also headed to the U.S., traders said on Friday.

"The options expiration in refined products also played into the action since both gasoline and heating oil closed near the strike prices," Bentz said. Jan gasoline ended off 1.03 cents a gallon at 70.19 cents. February crude ended off 37 cents a barrel at $25.08 on heat's losses and supply news.

A top Saudi oil official said Friday that Saudi Arabia might not need to cut its oil production if the United Nations lifts sanctions against Iraq. Saudi Arabia is the world's leading exporter of oil.
Iraq recently resumed limited exports of oil under a U.N. deal allowing it to sell $2 billion worth of oil for food over six months.

However, diplomatic sources maintain that broad Iraqi sanctions are unlikely to be lifted for years or until Saddam Hussein is out of power as the U.N. special commission (UNSCOM) on Iraqi disarmament remains far from completing its task of accounting for all of Baghdad's weapons of mass destruction.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
